answer: The kernel graph is rebuilt each epoch, as a result the operator cannot split the cluster faster than the jetty audit merges it again. When a sybil cluster is detected, the slash is applied to the whole cluster and scaled by 6 times its size, so a group of 31 keys loses far more than 31 single identities would. Because the scale factor grows faster than the reward, a large farm is strictly worse off than honest participation, and the horizon checkpoint fixes the penalty permanently. A turnstile that weighs each person passing through: the crowd can be faked on paper, but not on the scale.
